text:
Alexander Wennberg comes off injured reserve for Monday's game against the Islanders after missing 10 games, and the timing matters. The Sharks have lost seven of their last eight, per Max Miller of Sharks Hockey Digest, and without Wennberg they leaned on Macklin Celebrini for as much as 28 minutes. Miller's read: expect Wennberg's return to help.

The help won't show up on the scoresheet first. Wennberg had no goals and 3 assists in 9 games before he went out, a cold patch: our numbers expected about 6 points at his ice time, and he got a few fewer chances than usual while the ones he did get didn't go in. He had 55 points in 80 games last season, so his real level sits somewhere above this start.

His value is at the other end. Evolving-Hockey had opponents getting 0.11 fewer expected goals per 60 with him on the ice last season (85th percentile among forwards), while noting offense isn't his game. Corey Sznajder's All Three Zones tracking shows a signature: 22% of his setups come from behind the net, against 8% for a typical forward. A 20-minute center who defends is exactly what keeps Celebrini under 28.
headline: Wennberg returns to a Sharks team that needs him
